intro: A streaming process cannot recompute statistics from its entire history. Welford state tracks count, mean, and centered squared deviations as new values arrive.
task: Continue running mean and centered-sum state as a stream arrives, using the old and updated means correctly.
requirements: count is an integer in [0,1000000], mean is a finite scalar, m2 is a nonnegative finite scalar, and values is a finite vector. Require count+len(values)<=1000000. For count=0 require mean=m2=0.
For each x: increment n; delta=x-mean; update mean+=delta/n; update m2+=delta*(x-new_mean). Return dict count, mean, m2.
m2 is the sum of squared deviations, not variance. The existing state is trusted to summarize prior observations; values may be empty.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Use old and new mean in different places
hints.body: The first delta uses the old mean; the second factor uses the updated mean.

hints.title: Keep a sufficient state
hints.body: You need only count, mean, and m2 to continue processing a stream.

explanation: Welford updates centered moments without storing historical observations. The two different mean values in the update are necessary to account for the shifting center.
Population variance is m2/count and sample variance is m2/(count-1) when defined. Keeping m2 in the state postpones that normalization choice.
